The original has two unsupported claims: “10x more effective” and “trusted by everyone.” Rewrite: “Built to help [audience] achieve [supported outcome] using [documented capability]. See the product evidence and decide whether it fits your use case.” If you have a valid comparative study or trust/prevalence data, we can strengthen the claim within that evidence.

Decision: does adding claim-specific diagnostic proof improve the target action? Randomize eligible visitors to the same page with versus without the proof block; keep main claim, offer, CTA, and layout constant as feasible. Pre-register one primary outcome, guardrails, sample/stopping rule, and analysis. A conversion lift identifies the proof-block variant effect in this context; mechanism interpretation needs a construct-appropriate check.

Update a bounded message hypothesis and check targeting, placement, seasonality, offer, tracking, and other concurrent changes; use a randomized test if causal attribution matters.

A feature list is not enough to make a defensible value proposition because value depends on whose goal or burden the feature changes. Give me the audience + desired outcome (or the current alternative/problem). Until then, the safe structure is: “[capability] helps [specific audience] achieve/reduce [verified outcome/barrier], compared with [current alternative], supported by [evidence].” Do not fill the outcome with a guess.
